Euler & Hamilton Paths

Graph TheoryAlgorithmsLogic
Game: Walk through a graph using every line once, or visit every dot once.
How to play: Choose a graph and a path type, then click the dots in order. Back removes the last click.
Look for the math

Some walks are possible and some are not — and the two kinds of path obey entirely different rules.

Euler paths

An Euler path uses each edge exactly once. Euler's criterion says it exists precisely when the graph is connected and has either 0 or 2 vertices of odd degree; with 0 odd vertices the path closes into a cycle. The used edges vanish as you click, then return coloured when the path is complete.

Hamilton paths

A Hamilton path visits each vertex exactly once. There is no similarly simple criterion: finding one is a search problem. The logic test checks both validators on real and invalid walks and compares the existence tests with a brute-force search on small graphs.

Try the star in Euler mode. Can you explain why no path works there?
